result:
The change is complete. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (8 tests, 0 failures).

I turned on Japanese via the framework's built-in i18n rather than hand-rolling locale handling: `src/app.ts` now declares `i18n: { supported: ['en', 'ja'] }`, which mounts Guren's locale detection (query → cookie → `Accept-Language`, q-value sorted, base-language matched, falling back to `en`) and shares the resolved locale plus its catalog with Inertia pages. The login and register copy moved out of the components into a new `lang/en/auth.json` (verbatim English) with a mirrored `lang/ja/auth.json` carrying the exact Japanese strings from the request, and `lang/ja/messages.json` adds the Japanese welcome message `:nameへようこそ！` keeping its placeholder — `bunx guren check --i18n` reports full 20-key parity on both sides. `resources/js/pages/auth/Login.tsx` and `Register.tsx` now pull every label, the heading, subtitle, submit button, footer text, and the `<Head title>` through `useTranslation()`, and `LoginController`/`RegisterController` pass `this.t('auth.login.title')` / `this.t('auth.register.title')` as the Inertia document title so the browser-tab title is localized on both the SSR and non-SSR rendering paths (this makes the English non-SSR `<title>` "Sign in"/"Sign up", matching the documented English titles, instead of the previously unused "Login"/"Register" metadata). `.guren/translations.gen.ts` was regenerated by `bun run codegen`, and `tests/AuthLocale.test.ts` covers Japanese rendering for a Japanese browser, English for `en`, `en-US,en;q=0.9`, `en-US,en;q=0.9,ja;q=0.5`, `fr-FR,fr;q=0.9`, and no header at all, plus key and placeholder parity between the two catalogs; I verified the fully server-rendered output of both pages in both languages against a production build before removing the build artifacts.
